files.lesson.md: --- order: 43 unit: conditional10 node: AC9M10P01 n2 uses: [AC9M10P01 n1, AC9M9P02 n2] # the language of given; and / or from a Venn diagram connection: rare-test title: Tables, Venns and trees summary: "A two-way table, a Venn diagram and a tree can all show the same conditional chance. Read the chance off a table by looking inside the group it is given, and see why a test that is usually right can still be wrong most of the times it says positive." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A screening test comes back positive. Does that mean the person has the condition?" explainPicture: { ref: test.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Out of 1000 people, 67 test positive: 18 who have the condition and 49 who don't. The chance of the condition, given a positive test, is 18 out of 67." } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8441 url: http://127.0.0.1:8441/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- Doctors use screening tests on people who feel well. In this lesson, a test is made up for a rare condition. Every rate is made up: a real test's rates come from the people who make it, and a doctor looks them up. Of every 1000 people, 20 have the condition. The test is positive for 9 in 10 of the people who have it, and, wrongly, for 1 in 20 of those who don't. ## Predict: a positive result ```step stage: predict insight: "Many students take 'the test is right 9 in 10 times' as the answer. The people who test positive include many without the condition, because there are so many more of them." check: type: predict q: "1000 people take the test. Someone is told they tested positive. About how likely is it that this person really has the condition?" options: - "About 9 in 10" - "About 1 in 2" - "About 1 in 4" - "About 1 in 20" actual: "About 1 in 4. Of the 1000 people, 18 who have the condition test positive, and so do 49 of the 980 who don't. That is 67 positives, and 18 of them have the condition: 18/67 = 0.27." ``` Make a guess before you use the board. ## Run: the positives only ```step stage: run insight: "'Given a positive test' shrinks the whole to the 67 positives. The table and the Venn diagram show the same counts: the 18 who have the condition sit inside the 67." try: { playground: board, starter: "test.yml#run", height: 640 } check: { type: board, text: "The board shows the 1000 people, given a positive test. Choose the people who have the condition (Condition only and Condition and Positive). How many of the positives is that?", when: "g = 67 and h = 18" } ``` The table has the same four numbers as the diagram. Look down the Positive column: 18 and 49. Together they are the 67 who tested positive. ## Investigate: reading the table ```step stage: investigate insight: "Rates only become counts when you start from a group of people. Counting 1000 people through the rates builds the table, and the chance given a positive test is read inside the Positive column." tasks: - check: { type: number, q: "The test is positive for 18 people who have the condition and for 49 who don't. Out of the 1000 people, how many test positive?", answer: 67, tolerance: 0, feedback: [[18, "That is only the positives who have the condition. People without it can test positive too."], [49, "Those are the false alarms. Add the people who have the condition and test positive."]], explain: "18 + 49 = 67 people test positive." } smaller: check: { type: number, q: "20 of the 1000 people have the condition and the test is positive for 9 in 10 of them. How many of those 20 test positive?", answer: 18, tolerance: 0, explain: "9 in 10 of 20: 20 ÷ 10 × 9 = 18." } - check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A different screening test (made up). Of 1000 people, 50 have the condition. The test is positive for 45 of those 50 and, wrongly, for 38 of the 950 others. Given a positive test, what is the chance the person has the condition? Give a decimal to 2 places." steps: - ["All the positives: $45 + 38 = 83$", "the group the 'given' picks"] - ["Positives with the condition: $45$", "the count you want inside the group"] - ["$45 \\div 83 = 0.54$", "the part over the group"] answer: "0.54" answerLabel: "Chance" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["0.9", "That is 45 out of the 50 who have the condition: the chance of a positive test, given the condition. The group here is all the positives."] - ["0.05", "That is 45 out of all 1000 people. Given a positive test, divide by the positives."] criteria: - "I added the positives from both groups to find the group." - "I counted only the people with the condition inside it." - "I divided by the positives, not by 1000 or 50." explain: "83 people test positive, 45 of them have the condition: 45 ÷ 83 = 0.54. About 1 in 2." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#maya" text: "Maya finds the chance a person has the condition, given a positive test. Click the line where she goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: base-rate-ignored explain: "Line 3: 9 in 10 is the chance of a positive test, given the condition. She needs the chance of the condition, given a positive test, and the positives include 49 people without it: 18 out of 67." ``` ### Fill in the table Build the table from the rates by starting with a group of 1000 people. ### Given a positive test A table, a Venn diagram and a tree all show the same four counts. Here is how to read the chance off a table. ```worked \text{A scanner checks 1000 phone cases (made up). 40 are faulty.} :: Start from a group and sort it by the two things: faulty or not, flagged or not. 36 \text{ faulty cases are flagged; } 48 \text{ of the } 960 \text{ good cases are flagged too} :: Fill in the table from the rates: the flagged column holds 36 and 48. 36 + 48 = 84 \text{ cases are flagged} :: "Given a flag" picks this group. P(\text{faulty} \mid \text{flagged}) = \tfrac{36}{84} = \tfrac{3}{7} :: The faulty cases inside the group, over the group. ``` Now try one on paper first, with the example beside you. This test is also made up. Then type your answer. ### Find the mistake Read Maya's working. Does 9 in 10 answer the question that is asked? ## Modify: change the test ```step stage: modify insight: "A tree shows the same four counts as the table, with each branch's chance on it. Changing the test changes the false alarms and so the chance given a positive. At the edge, with no false alarms, every positive is real." try: { playground: board, starter: "test.yml#tree", height: 640 } tasks: - starter: "test.yml#tree" hint: ["Click the two outcomes with a Positive test.", "Positive on the Yes branch is 18 people. Positive on the No branch is 49."] check: { type: board, text: "This tree is the same test. Choose both outcomes where the test is Positive. How many of the 1000 are in your event?", when: "n = 67 and m = 1000", explain: "18 + 49 = 67 of the 1000. Each branch shows its chance: 1/50 have the condition, and 9/10 of them test positive." } - starter: "test.yml#better" hint: "Choose the two positive outcomes on the tree to find the number of positives, then divide the condition's positives by it." check: { type: answer, q: "This test gives fewer false alarms: 14 of the 980 people without the condition test positive. Given a positive test, what is the chance the person has the condition? (Decimal to 2 places.)", answer: "0.56", feedback: [["0.27", "That is for the first test, with 49 false alarms."], ["0.9", "That is the chance of a positive test, given the condition."]], explain: "The positives are 18 + 14 = 32, and 18 of them have the condition: 18/32 = 0.56." } - starter: "test.yml#nofalse" hint: "The No branch has no Positive leaf, so the tree drops it." check: type: question q: "Edge case: a test with no false alarms. Nobody without the condition tests positive. Given a positive test, what is the chance the person has the condition?" options: ["1: every positive is a person with the condition", "0.9, the chance the test catches the condition", "0.5, because it is either positive or negative", "It cannot be worked out because there is no Positive branch on one side"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "0.9 is the chance of a positive, given the condition. Given a positive, the group is the 18 people with it.", "A person is not equally likely to be either. Count the positives.", "The group is the positives, and there are 18 of them, all with the condition."] explain: "The only positives are the 18 who have the condition, so 18 out of 18 is 1." ``` ### The tree ### A better test ### No false alarms ## Practise: reading the table ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading a chance given a group from counts, and keeping the two directions apart. Review: and / or from Year 9." tasks: - check: { type: number, q: "Of 1000 people (made up), 100 have a condition. The test is positive for 90 of them and wrongly for 90 of the 900 others. Given a positive test, what is the chance the person has the condition? Give a decimal.", answer: 0.5, tolerance: 0.01, feedback: [[0.9, "That is 90 out of the 100 with the condition. Given a positive test, the group is 90 + 90 = 180."]], explain: "180 people test positive and 90 have the condition: 90 ÷ 180 = 0.5." } - check: { type: number, q: "Using the lesson's counts (18 have the condition and test positive, 2 have it and test negative, 49 don't have it and test positive, 931 don't and test negative), what is the chance of a positive test, given the person has the condition? Give a decimal.", answer: 0.9, tolerance: 0.01, feedback: [[0.27, "That is the chance of the condition, given a positive test. Here the group is the 20 people with the condition."]], explain: "The group is the 20 people with the condition and 18 test positive: 18 ÷ 20 = 0.9." } - check: { type: number, q: "Review: of 100 people, 55 play sport, 30 play music and 10 play both. How many play neither?", answer: 25, tolerance: 0, feedback: [[15, "The 10 who play both were taken off twice. Add them back once."]], explain: "55 + 30 − 10 = 75 play something, so 100 − 75 = 25 play neither." } ``` ### Given a positive ### Given the condition ### A review From Year 9: take the overlap off once. That count is not given anything, so the whole stays at everyone. ## Make: back to the positive test ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the opening: fill in a table for 1000 people from the rates, then say what a positive result means. A good answer gives the number and puts it in words with the group." tasks: - check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Back to the screening test: 20 of every 1000 people have the condition, the test is positive for 9 in 10 of them, and wrongly positive for 1 in 20 of the others. Fill in a table for 1000 people on paper, then find the chance of the condition, given a positive test. Give a decimal to 2 places." steps: - ["With the condition: $20$, of whom $18$ test positive", "9 in 10 of 20"] - ["Without it: $980$, of whom $49$ test positive", "1 in 20 of 980"] - ["$18 \\div (18 + 49) = 18 \\div 67 = 0.27$", "the condition's positives over all the positives"] answer: "0.27" answerLabel: "Chance" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["0.9", "That is the chance of a positive test, given the condition. The question is the other way round."] - ["0.02", "That is the chance of the condition before the test. A positive test is a clue: use the positives as the group."] criteria: - "I filled in the table from the rates starting with 1000 people." - "I used the positives as the group." - "I divided the condition's positives by all the positives." explain: "18 of the 67 positives have the condition: 0.27. Most positives are false alarms, because so many more people don't have the condition." - check: type: question q: "Which sentence best explains the result to a friend who tested positive?" options: ["About 1 in 4 people who test positive have the condition, because the condition is rare and many people without it also test positive, so a second test is a good idea", "The test is right 9 times out of 10, so you almost certainly have it", "A positive test means you do not have it", "The test is no good because it is sometimes wrong"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "9 in 10 is the chance of a positive test, given the condition. It is not the chance of the condition, given a positive test.", "A positive test does raise the chance: from 2 in 100 to about 27 in 100.", "The test is useful: it raises the chance a lot. It just does not decide it."] explain: "The chance rises from 2 in 100 before the test to about 27 in 100, which is a lot, but it does not decide. A good report gives the group it is given." ``` ### The table Work this out on paper first, then type your answer. ### What to tell a friend Sources: every rate and count in this lesson is made up (the condition, the test, the scanner and the sport counts). A real test's rates come from the people who make it, and a doctor looks them up. **Also used in** - **Quality control.** A scanner that flags faulty items has false alarms too, so a flag is a clue and not a verdict. - **Security checks.** An alarm that goes off sometimes without a reason has the same table. - **Next lesson.** Deciding whether one thing changes the chance of another. ```teacher summary: Students fill in a two-way table for 1000 people from stated rates, read the chance of the condition given a positive test inside the Positive column, and see the same four counts as a Venn diagram and a tree. The context is a made-up screening test for a rare condition (AC9M10P01, node 2). time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 18 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 14 min goals: - I can build a two-way table from rates by starting with a group of people. - I can read a chance given a group off a table, a Venn diagram or a tree. - I can say why a test that is usually right can be wrong most of the time it says positive. struggle: "Taking 'right 9 times in 10' as the chance given a positive. Ask: 'Of all the people who tested positive, who are they?'" before: > Do the Run board and the tree yourself first. Students need the last lesson (given). The one idea: start from a group of 1000, turn each rate into a count, and read the chance inside the group the "given" picks. The tree shows the same four counts: each first branch is the share of 1000, each second branch is the share of its own group (that is the conditional chance on the branch), and the numbers at the leaves are the counts. Multiplying along a branch is shown by the branch labels and the counts agreeing, not taught as a rule here. Every rate is made up: 2 in 100 have the condition, 9 in 10 of them test positive, 1 in 20 of the others do. They are chosen so 1000 people give whole counts (18, 2, 49, 931). Say clearly that real test rates come from the maker and a doctor looks them up; no real condition is named on purpose. The surprising answer (about 1 in 4) is the point. It depends on how rare the condition is. Do the Modify board to see it move: with fewer false alarms the chance rises to 0.56; with none it is 1. running: - "Predict: show of hands. Most students choose 'about 9 in 10'." - "Run: ask students to say the group out loud: the positives, not the 1000." - "Paper: the scanner is worked first as the example. The second test and the Make table are worked on paper first. Look for the table and the group named in the first line." - "Modify: ask for a prediction before each board: will the chance go up or down?" stuck: - see: A student answers 0.9 for the chance of the condition given a positive. ask: Which of the 1000 people tested positive? Are they all people with the condition? fix: Count all the positives, 18 + 49, and use that as the group. - see: A student divides by 1000. ask: Once you know the test was positive, which people are still possible? fix: Cross out everyone who tested negative. The 67 left are the whole. - see: A student gets 49 false alarms by taking 1 in 20 of 1000. ask: "Who can be wrongly positive: people with the condition or without it?" fix: "Only the 980 without the condition: 980 ÷ 20 = 49." stretch: Find the chance of having the condition, given a negative test. What does a negative result tell you? Then ask what would happen to the chance given a positive if the condition were twice as common. support: A blank table with the row and column totals already filled in (20, 980, 67, 933). The student fills the four inside cells. leads: > Continues AC9M10P01 node 2. Where it leads: deciding whether two events are independent, and simulating a conditional chance (the lessons after this one). exit: q: A test is positive for 8 of the 10 people who have a condition and for 5 of the 90 who don't. Given a positive test, what is the chance a person has it? a: 8 out of 13 positives, 8/13 = 0.62. explain: > A conditional chance is read from a table, Venn diagram or tree by looking only at the group that is given. - Start from a group of 1000 and turn each rate into a count. - "Given a positive test" means the group is everyone who tested positive, with and without the condition. - The chance is the condition's positives over all the positives. - A rare condition means most of the positives can be false alarms, even from a good test. sources: - title: "Made up for this lesson: the 1000 people, the condition, the test and its rates, the phone-case scanner and the sport counts. A real test's rates come from its maker and a doctor looks them up." url: https://tutorials.learningwaypoints.com/maths/data/tables-venns-trees/ checked: 2026-10-25 ```

# Boards for "Tables, Venns and trees". A screening test for a rare condition, 1000 people (all rates made up):
# 20 have the condition; the test is positive for 18 of them and wrongly positive for 49 of the 980 others.
# Venn counts are in the order: condition only (tests negative), both (condition and positive), positive only, neither.

# region: run
widget: venn
labels: Condition, Positive
counts: 2, 18, 49, 931
given: b
# endregion

# region: tree
widget: events
first: Yes, No
second: Positive, Negative
names: Condition, Test
weights: 18, 2; 49, 931
view: tree
# endregion

# region: better
widget: events
first: Yes, No
second: Positive, Negative
names: Condition, Test
weights: 18, 2; 14, 966
view: tree
# endregion

# region: nofalse
widget: events
first: Yes, No
second: Positive, Negative
names: Condition, Test
weights: 18, 2; 0, 980
view: tree
# endregion

# region: explain-pic
widget: events
first: Yes, No
second: Positive, Negative
names: Condition, Test
weights: 18, 2; 49, 931
view: tree
event: b = Positive
choose: off
# endregion
files.working.txt:
# Maya's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: maya
The test says positive. I want the chance the person has the condition.
Of the 20 people who have it, 18 test positive. That is 9 in 10.
So the chance of having the condition, given a positive test, is 9 in 10 = 0.9.
That means a positive result is right nine times out of ten.
# endregion
